issues.legal_issue: A villagers’ right to graze cattle on estate land is an encumbrance within the statutory definition and is extinguished when the estate vests in the State free from encumbrances.
material_facts: An estate containing grassland used by villagers for cattle grazing vested in the State under a notification.
The villagers claimed that their pasturage right continued after vesting and sought an injunction against interference with its exercise.

The governing law defined encumbrances broadly to include rights or interests of whatever nature relating to estate land or its produce, subject to specified exceptions, and provided for vesting free from encumbrances.
issues.conclusion: The grazing right is an encumbrance within the definition and was extinguished upon vesting; the appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(h) of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953, an encumbrance includes all rights or interests of whatever nature relating to land comprised in an estate or its produce, apart from the stated exclusions. Sections 4 and 5 provide for vesting free from all encumbrances. The Court applied the statutory language in light of the Act’s land-reform objective and held that the definition’s broad reach could not be cut down. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

rule.if: estate_vesting_dispute and grazing_right_relates_to_estate_land and definition_covers_all_related_interests and estate_vests_free_of_encumbrances

predicates.estate_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a right survives the vesting of an estate in the State under a land-reform scheme.
predicates.grazing_right_relates_to_estate_land: Villagers claim a right to graze cattle on land comprised in the estate.
predicates.definition_covers_all_related_interests: The governing law includes rights or interests of whatever nature relating to estate land or its produce within its definition of encumbrances, subject to stated exclusions.
predicates.estate_vests_free_of_encumbrances: The governing law provides that the estate vests in the State free from encumbrances.

issues.definition: When an estate-vesting dispute concerns a grazing right related to estate land, and the governing law broadly covers related interests and provides for vesting free from encumbrances, the grazing right is extinguished on vesting.

issues.legal_issue: A fluctuating body of villagers claiming a collective grazing right falls within the statutory expression covering intermediaries or other persons.
material_facts: Villagers brought a representative action asserting that the agrarian community had enjoyed a right to graze cattle on estate land.
The claim concerned a collective and changing group of villagers rather than identified individuals.
The statutory definition referred to rights or interests belonging to intermediaries or other persons.
issues.conclusion: The villagers are other persons within the statutory definition, and the collective or fluctuating character of the group does not exclude their grazing right from it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(h) of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953, covers rights or interests belonging to intermediaries or other persons. The Court construed other persons to mean persons other than intermediaries and found no basis in the text or statutory purpose for limiting the phrase to particular, definite, known individuals. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.estate_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a claimed right is covered by the definition governing estate vesting.
predicates.villagers_claim_collective_grazing_right: Villagers assert collectively that they have a right to graze cattle on estate land.
predicates.definition_covers_intermediaries_and_oth: The governing law refers to rights or interests belonging to intermediaries or other persons.

issues.definition: When villagers collectively claim a grazing right in an estate-vesting dispute and the governing definition covers intermediaries or other persons, the collective villagers are other persons.

issues.legal_issue: A customary grazing right contrary to the statutory vesting scheme does not survive the scheme’s override of contrary usage or custom.
material_facts: The villagers asserted that their pasturage right had been enjoyed as a customary right.
The law provided that its provisions operated notwithstanding any contrary usage or custom.
The estate vested in the State free from encumbrances under the statutory scheme.
issues.conclusion: The customary character of the grazing right does not preserve it against the statutory scheme; the right does not survive vesting.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act, 1953, provides that the Act operates notwithstanding any contrary usage or custom. Sections 4 and 5 provide for vesting of the estate and intermediary rights free from encumbrances. The Court held that a customary grazing right that limits the rights vested under that scheme cannot prevail against it. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.estate_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns the effect of an estate-vesting scheme on a claimed right.
predicates.grazing_right_claimed_as_custom: Villagers claim that their grazing right arises from usage or custom.
predicates.law_overrides_contrary_custom: The governing law provides that it operates notwithstanding contrary usage or custom.
predicates.estate_vests_free_of_encumbrances: The governing law provides that the estate vests in the State free from encumbrances.

issues.definition: When a grazing right is claimed as custom in an estate-vesting dispute, and the governing law overrides contrary custom and provides for vesting free from encumbrances, the customary grazing right does not survive vesting.
